> 江海所以能為百谷王者，以其善下之.

Chapter 65 said: don't light the room. Chapter 66 says where to stand instead.

The chapter closes on the most slogan-like line in the book — 以其不爭，故天下莫能與之爭 — and inside it is a character that has been read wrong for two thousand years, quietly.

## 厭 is a sated animal under a cliff

厭: 笮也 — 笮 means to press, to squeeze.

The character is built from 厂 (the cliff) and 猒 (sated — 飽也, an animal that has eaten full).

An animal, full, pressed under an overhang.

Full and pressed. That is 厭.

## 天下樂推而不厭

Not "the world gladly raises him up and does not dislike him." It is: the world gladly raises him, and does not feel pressed.

厭 is not an emotion. It is a bodily sensation — the sense of weight on you.

## The three lines are one measurement

- 處上而民不重 — above them, and the people do not feel heavy.
- 處前而民不害 — ahead of them, and the people are not diminished.
- 樂推而不厭 — raised up, and no one feels pressed.

重, 害, 厭 — three words for load. The chapter is not describing a humble person. It is reporting a measurement: stand as high and as far forward as you like, and check what the people underneath register.

The real keyword is not 不爭. It is 輕 — light.

## 王 is where people go

王: 天下所歸往也 — where all under heaven return to and go toward.

Not "to rule." To be headed for.

And 說文 on 海: 以納百川者 — the one that takes in the hundred streams.

Two definitions, one structure: the low place is where the water arrives.

## 谷 is a spring running out into a river

谷: 泉出通川為谷 — a spring issuing and opening into a rivercourse.

So 百谷王 is not "king of the valleys" as a title of rank. It is the place where a hundred springs, having become streams, all end up.

## 欲上民，必以言下之；欲先民，必以身後之

To be above, put your words below. To be ahead, put your body behind.

The exchange is precise and it is not symbolic. Words are what a position issues; putting the words below means the position does not open with commands. The body is what occupies space; putting it behind means the front is left to others.

## 以其不爭，故天下莫能與之爭

Because he does not contend, no one under heaven can contend with him.

The mechanism is structural, not moral. Contention requires two parties facing each other. The one who has taken the lower position is not facing anyone — he is where everyone is already heading.

Which is why the claim is not "he wins." It is: 莫能與之爭 — there is no one to contend with. The contest has no second participant.

## Why this follows 65

65 removed the spotlight, which is what creates the contest in the first place.
66 puts the person where the light doesn't reach: downstream, low, behind.

And the result is not invisibility. It is that the weight stops being felt — which is the only durable form of standing high.

## A test

Take a position where you lead — a team, a project, a family. Ask three people underneath, not whether they like you, but whether anything feels heavy. The answer is the chapter's only instrument.
